name: Theresa May
role: British Conservative politician: Home Secretary (2010-2016), Prime Minister (2016-2019), MP for Maidenhead (1997-2024)
summary: A one-nation Conservative who combined support for free markets and trade with an active state role in industry, workers' protections and energy prices. As Home Secretary and Prime Minister she backed strong security powers and tighter immigration control, took Britain out of the EU while insisting on an outward-looking country, and backed same-sex marriage and net-zero emissions. Many economic, liberty and cultural questions have no recorded position.

abortion-legal.rationale: Stated that it is absolutely right a woman should have the right to a safe and legal abortion, leaving Northern Ireland to its Assembly.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Presented bringing the deficit down as a core achievement and attacked borrowing hundreds of billions as reckless.

class-collaboration.rationale: Called for a social contract between employers and the people who work for them and rejected social division.

collective-defense.rationale: Committed fully to NATO and called it the cornerstone of British defence.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The manifesto pledges to confront the burning injustice of racial disparity and to mandate changes to stop and search.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Told the Commons that laws criminalising same-sex relations across the Commonwealth are a discriminatory legacy she deeply regrets and wants reformed.

death-penalty.rationale: Stated the UK's long-standing position that it calls for the abolition of the death penalty globally.

decide-locally.rationale: The manifesto says her government devolved more power to English local authorities, closer to local people, and would consolidate devolution.

democracy-best.rationale: Though a Remain voter, she insisted on delivering the 2016 referendum result and warned that ignoring it would be a con trick on the British people.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said every person, no matter their gender, should have an equal voice in the democracy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Her government legislated the 2050 net-zero emissions target, the first by a G7 economy, acting on the Committee on Climate Change's advice.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Called NATO the cornerstone of defence and committed fully to the alliance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Told the Commons that criminalising same-sex relations is inconsistent with the common value of equality and denounced homophobic hatred after Orlando.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The manifesto backs shale gas extraction and pledges changes to planning law for shale applications.

expand-nuclear.rationale: As PM she took the decision to proceed with Hinkley Point C and told the Commons nuclear should keep a role in the energy mix.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered the 2018 strikes without Security Council approval, after Russia vetoed action, with the Cabinet judging them legal.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The manifesto promises ministerial scrutiny and control over foreign ownership of critical infrastructure such as civil nuclear, telecoms, defence and energy.

free-trade.rationale: Described Britain as the world's leading advocate for free markets and free trade and set out to pursue new trade agreements.

future-generations.rationale: The manifesto pledges to be the first generation to leave the environment in a better state than it inherited.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The manifesto commits to retain the Trident continuous-at-sea nuclear deterrent as the ultimate guarantee of security.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Her words point both ways: the free market is the greatest agent of human progress (2017), yet the manifesto rejects untrammelled free markets and she would step in to repair them (2016).

nation-first.rationale: Her words split: she rejected the 'citizen of the world' outlook (2016) yet insisted that Brexit meant a global, outward-looking Britain, not a retreat.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The manifesto calls for positive, active government on health, social care, housing and industry, far beyond protection from violence.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended a parliamentary democracy in which every person has an equal voice and elections are not rigged.

open-borders.rationale: Said Britain is not leaving the EU to give up control of immigration and that free movement will end once and for all.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Took Britain out of the EU, saying it would be a fully sovereign and independent country again.

proportional-representation.rationale: The manifesto commits to retain first past the post for parliamentary elections and extend it to police and mayoral elections.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Her manifesto promised a decent living wage rising to 60 per cent of median earnings and she cited the national living wage as her government's work for the low paid.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Her programme sets net migration in the tens of thousands and ends free movement, while keeping skilled migration.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The manifesto defends pooling and sharing resources across the four nations through the Barnett Formula.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Said her party is not afraid to hold businesses to account, pledged fairer corporate governance and cited the energy price cap her government introduced.

rehabilitation.rationale: The manifesto says prisons should be places of reform and rehabilitation but also that incarceration is punishment for serious crime.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Her manifesto pledged action against hate speech online with platform duties and take-down, and a plan to tackle hate crime.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Declared dogma and ideology dangerous and backed free schools not because ideology says so but because they work.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The manifesto commits to maintain spending 0.7 per cent of national income on aid to end extreme poverty.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposed a second Scottish independence referendum, calling for Scotland within the United Kingdom, and pledged no divisive referendum at this time.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She voted for equal marriage and her government passed the 2013 Act; the Act enables same-sex marriage in England and Wales.

second-chamber.rationale: The manifesto keeps the House of Lords as a revising and scrutinising chamber and rules out comprehensive reform.

social-market-economy.rationale: Backed free markets but stepping in to repair them, with a public safety net and a protected NHS.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The manifesto sets a modern industrial strategy with strategic national investments and state-backed Future Britain funds.

state-harmful.rationale: Argued for positive, active government that steps up rather than back, and government as a force for good.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As Home Secretary she introduced and carried the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, with bulk interception powers (Part 6) for national security and serious crime.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Told the Commons she wants WTO reform rather than states resorting to tariffs in trade disputes.

total-state.rationale: The manifesto says government alone cannot solve every challenge and that business and citizens' duties carry society.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called the NHS a vital national institution reflecting fairness and said her party upheld its founding principles.

voter-id.rationale: The manifesto she led pledged to legislate so that a form of identification must be presented before voting.

women-suffrage.rationale: Described a democracy where every person, no matter their gender, has an equal voice.

notes: Pass of 2026-11-15 (rules 7). Evidence: her Hansard speeches 1997-2024 (local corpus, searched by theme keywords), party programme and conference speeches as leader, Lancaster House speech, the 2018 Syria statement, and the texts of the acts and order cited. Themes searched: markets and trade, welfare and wages, surveillance, immigration, equality and marriage, abortion, defence and the UN, nuclear and climate, devolution and Scotland, elections and the Lords, drugs, firearms, prisons, hate crime, encryption. Commons votes were not available (no division corpus), so same-sex marriage rests on the Act and her own statement that she voted for it. Her 2016 Syria-strike decision is scored on the act, not the speech. Policies as Home Secretary such as the 2014 and 2016 Immigration Acts, the Psychoactive Substances Act and the Modern Slavery Act were not opened in a readable source and are not used. Her later Modern Slavery speeches (2023) are not used for any statement.
